extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and scientists invited to peer review manuscripts for PLOS Biology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers performing peer review for PLOS Biology, covering invitation acceptance, conduct, what to assess in different article types (including preregistered studies and magazine pieces), and journal policies on confidentiality, conflicts, and published peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept invitation only if qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept an invitation only if you have the knowledge, time and objectivity necessary to provide an unbiased assessment of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the links in the invitation email to accept or decline; if you accept you also give permission to publish your review under a Creative Commons Attribution CC BY license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model and signing option
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Biology practices single-anonymized peer review by default (you will know authors' names but your name will not be shared). Reviewers may choose to sign their name to their review when submitting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you sign, authors and other reviewers will see your name; if authors publish peer review history your name will accompany comments only if you chose to sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer cross-commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a full set of reviewer reports has been received, reports will be circulated anonymously among the reviewer panel to allow commenting on peers' reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will be given 2 working days to comment so as not to delay decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable reviews / transmission to other journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews may accompany manuscripts transferred to other PLOS journals or be transmitted to other journals at authors' request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS will contact individual reviewers for permission to transmit their names; reports are otherwise transmitted anonymously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing interest is anything that interferes with or could be perceived as potentially interfering with a thorough and objective assessment (e.g., recent/current collaboration, direct competition, opportunity to profit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept a review assignment if you have a competing interest or cannot be objective. If unsure, contact the journal office. If requested to review despite a conflict, declare it when submitting your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit collaborators who helped the review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you had help completing the review you must share your collaborator’s name with the journal when you submit the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the name in the question 'Did you prepare this review with someone else?' or email the journal. Do not include collaborator names in the text of the review itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep manuscripts and correspondence confidential and do not share information about submissions with anyone else unless previously agreed with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make use of material or take advantage of information gained through the peer review process; read the PLOS Confidentiality Policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose prior reviews of the same manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: If you reviewed the article at another journal, let the editor know via email and consider the manuscript as a new submission unless instructed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind the manuscript may have been revised and PLOS Biology’s criteria for publication may differ from the other journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to complete your review within 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time, email the journal as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer credit via ORCID/Publons
rubrics_metrics.description: Link your PLOS reviewer account to ORCID or Publons to have reviewer activity posted to your ORCID profile review activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This confirms you completed a review for the journal but does not publish the content of your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the editors with an expert opinion regarding the validity and quality of the manuscript and supply authors with explicit feedback on how to improve their paper to be acceptable for publication in PLOS Biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write clearly, addressing the specific evaluative points listed by the journal (claims, novelty, evidence, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct and scientific validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be ethically conducted and scientifically valid to be eligible for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise any concerns about publication ethics, research ethics, or data availability directly with journal staff (plosbiology@plos.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be original as part of being exceptional for publication in PLOS Biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are not novel, specify papers that weaken originality; note the complementary research policy if similar work was recently published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance to researchers in its field
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be important to researchers in its specific field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how significant the main claims are for the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest to scientists outside the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should be of interest beyond its immediate subfield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate who would find the paper of interest and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous methodology and substantial evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must use rigorous methodology and provide substantial evidence for its conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether data and analyses fully support the claims, whether methods are sufficient for reproducibility, and whether additional work is needed (how much and how difficult).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify main claims and assess their significance
rubrics_metrics.description: State what the main claims of the paper are and how significant they are for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the claims and their impact; discuss whether the paper is outstanding and why or why not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess novelty and cite contradictory prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims novel? If not, specify papers that weaken the claims of originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If similar work exists, evaluate eligibility under the complementary research policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place claims in context of previous literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the claims are properly placed in the context of previous literature and whether the authors have treated the literature fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out omissions or misrepresentations of prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition and accession numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Original data should be deposited in appropriate repositories with accession/version numbers provided for genes, proteins, mutants, diseases, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check compliance with PLOS’ data availability policy and request repository deposition where absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript organization and accessibility to non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the manuscript is well organized and written clearly enough to be accessible to non-specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend edits to improve clarity and accessibility where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological detail and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Details of the methodology should be sufficient to allow experiments to be reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend publishing detailed protocols/algorithms as supporting information when warranted; if protocols are provided, ask authors to explain important deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend when additional work or protocols are needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify if any particular methods warrant detailed protocols online and whether deviations from protocols are adequately explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether additional experiments would improve the paper and estimate difficulty and value of those experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing/suppression policy for reviewer reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors do not delete reviewer reports; PLOS staff will not change reviewer comments except where language is inappropriate, contains confidential information, or would pose a major risk if conveyed to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, staff will discuss wording with reviewer before changes; otherwise minimal edits will be made. Comments may be marked as not needing to be addressed in revisions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision process and handling conflicting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors make the final decision based on reviewers' comments, the PLOS Biology criteria for publication, and their own assessment; conflicting reviews may prompt sharing reports among reviewers for further comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are not necessarily by majority rule; experts may disagree and editors weigh recommendations alongside other material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 (Preregistered Research Article) assessment: importance and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: For Stage 1 protocols, assess the importance of the research question(s) and whether the logic, rationale, and plausibility of the proposed hypotheses are valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the manuscript provides a valid rationale with clearly identified and justified research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 assessment: soundness and feasibility of methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the soundness and feasibility of the methodology and analysis pipeline, including statistical power analysis where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is the protocol technically sound and planned to lead to a meaningful outcome and allow testing of the stated hypotheses?

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 assessment: methodological detail for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the clarity and degree of methodological detail are sufficient to exactly replicate the proposed experimental procedures and analysis pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag missing detail that would prevent exact replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 assessment: outcome-neutral tests and quality checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether authors have pre-specified sufficient outcome-neutral tests (e.g., positive controls and quality checks) to ensure results can test the stated hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend additional checks if needed to validate future data collection and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 (Preregistered Research Article) assessment: adherence to Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: For Stage 2 manuscripts, assess whether the introduction, rationale and stated hypotheses are the same as the approved Stage 1 Protocol and whether authors adhered precisely to the approved Stage 1 experimental procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the appropriateness of any deviations and whether data satisfy the approved outcome-neutral conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 assessment: conclusions and post-hoc analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the authors' conclusions are justified given the data and whether any post-hoc analyses are justified, methodologically sound, and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure post-hoc analyses are clearly labeled and their justification is explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 assessment: data availability and timestamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Check, in accordance with PLOS’ data availability policy, that data has been made freely available in a public repository and time-stamped to show data was collected after Stage 1 Protocol approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data files should be appropriately time stamped to prevent pre-approval data collection being used to claim preregistration compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance not the basis for Stage 2 decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions for Stage 2 will not be based on the perceived importance or novelty of the Stage 2 results because significance was assessed during Stage 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus Stage 2 review on adherence to protocol and accuracy of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine submissions: general expectation of rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Magazine section articles are less formal than research articles but the science and logic are expected to be rigorous and precise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply appropriate standards of scientific accuracy and clarity despite a less formal format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspectives: grounded and persuasive opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspectives should address science-policy or science-society interfaces, present policy positions or examine publishing practices; they are opinion pieces but must be grounded in scientific reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess soundness of the science, coherence of argument, interest, significance, whether the point of view is well-argued and scientifically supportable, and suggest specific improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Pages: openness and avoidance of self-promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Community Pages highlight resources, tools, or initiatives that must be open and accessible to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess soundness of the science and coherence; ensure the piece avoids self-promotion and suggest improvements or encourage revision if potential exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essays: novel perspective and argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Essays should offer a provocative or novel perspective, outline the topic, clearly state and argue the viewpoint, and provide selected examples where applicable, while being grounded in scientific reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate interest, significance, and scientific support for the viewpoint; recommend specific suggestions to improve scope or interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolved Mysteries: stimulate research on poorly understood topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsolved Mystery articles should discuss a biological or medical topic that is poorly understood and in need of research attention, intended to stimulate future research outside authors' areas of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess soundness of the science and coherence; evaluate interest and whether the piece encourages new research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus Views: independence, balance, and actionable recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consensus View articles present comprehensive analysis by an independent, usually multidisciplinary, panel of experts who make specific recommendations on important issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect articles to be firmly grounded in scientific reality, balanced, and to offer clear, specific recommendations.
